subject: EdgeHealth private deployment — peering readout & latency commitments
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Voronova <elena@edgehealth.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment call — quick readout & ask

Hi Elena / EdgeHealth team,

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on goals. Quick recap and concrete asks so we keep momentum: 

Summary (per the call)
- Target latency: 50 ms p95 client-to-model for streaming token responses (we agreed to prioritize streaming tail latency).
- Throughput: baseline 350–400 RPS sustained for the initial phase, with burst capacity to 800 RPS during peak batch conversions.
- Concurrency: support for ~100 concurrent active streaming sessions; open to phased increase after initial validation.
- Egress preference: peer-to-peer (VPN/DirectConnect) into your VPC; avoid public egress.

What we need from you to qualify network path and SLOs:
1) Preferred peering method (VPN vs DirectConnect/Partner Express) and public IP ranges or BGP ASN we should expect.
2) One 2-hour window next week where your NOC can run continuous TCP traceroutes and capture 1 minute of packet-level pcap during a controlled load (we'll provide test endpoints).
3) Sample payload: if you have expected average token sizes / message rates per session, send an example — this helps size KV-cache and batching.

Attachments: edgehealth-private-arch-v1.pdf (diagram), sample-traces-0308.zip (tiny traces from our staging).

Next steps (proposed):
- Elena: confirm peering option + available test window by EOD Friday PST.
- Redwood (Marcus / Karthik / me): provision a scoped test endpoint and a short test plan (we'll share before the window).

If any of the targets above are unrealistic on your side, call them out and we'll propose alternatives (e.g., 60–75 ms p95 if traffic must traverse additional proxies).

Thanks — Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
https://www.redwood.ai
From: Elena Voronova <elena@edgehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeHealth IT Ops <it_ops@edgehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 16:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment call — quick readout & ask

Hi Tessa,

Appreciate the crisp recap. Confirming a few items from our side:
- Peering: we'll use AWS DirectConnect to our VPC (primary), with an IPSec VPN failover. We want traffic to remain internal — no public internet egress from our side.
- IP ranges: I'll share the CIDR list and the DirectConnect public prefixes in a separate email to your ops alias. Expect 3 /23 blocks and one BGP ASN (AS64555).
- Test window: can do Tue 21 Mar 09:00–11:00 PT (NOC will be on standby). That works best for our network team.
- Payloads: typical session is chat-based, avg 140 tokens per turn, bursts up to 600 tokens when users paste documents. Concurrent session mix skews heavier on short sessions — concurrency profile included in attached CSV.

Attached: edgehealth-network-scope.csv (includes CIDRs and a brief concurrency histogram).

A couple of asks for Redwood before the window:
1) Please provide an exact IP + port for your test endpoint and any required client certs for mutual TLS.
2) A short runbook we can hand to NOC with steps to start/stop the capture and what success looks like.

I'll loop in our infra lead (it_ops) on the follow-ups. Looking forward to the test.

Best,
Elena
Director, Platform Engineering | EdgeHealth
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 02:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment call — quick readout & ask

Thanks for the details — good signal. A few notes from infra/serving side before we lock the test plan: 

Quick assessment
- If EdgeHealth uses DirectConnect with a VPC endpoint in the same region as our dedicated pool, 50 ms p95 client-to-model (for streaming) is achievable in our tests, assuming minimal middleboxes and MTU intact across path.
- If traffic traverses an additional intermediary (e.g., an on-prem proxy with TLS re-termination), expect tail increases; plan for 60–75 ms p95 as a realistic contingency.

Test plan items we'll deliver (attachment: redwood-net-test-plan.md)
- Provision ephemeral test endpoint (mutual TLS) + detailed port/IPs.
- Load profile generator to emulate 100 concurrent streams with a 140-token average and bursts to 600 tokens.
- Continuous traceroute + packet captures on both sides for correlation.
- A small set of streaming-token-level latency metrics (client send -> first token, token-to-token pacing, final token e2e).

Operational asks for the run
- Confirm MTU path (if fragmentation occurs, it kills streaming perf).
- Ensure Symmetric routing for test window or tell us where asymmetric hops will be — we can still correlate but it complicates pcap pairing.
- Provide NTP time-sync verification on capture hosts.

I'll create a short JIRA (INF-9831) to track tasks and assign owners; Marcus will own endpoint provisioning, Karthik will own test harness, and I'll be on-point for packet correlation.

On the contingency front: if we observe >75 ms p95 during the test, next steps are: 1) validate MTU and proxy behaviour, 2) enable prefix caching and increase batch size while lowering per-request concurrency to control tail, 3) consider a dedicated ginger path (bypass proxies) during peak.

-Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Voronova <elena@edgehealth.com>, EdgeHealth IT Ops <it_ops@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment call — quick readout & ask

Perfect — thanks everyone for the speed. Final checklist & owners before the test on Tue 21 Mar 09:00 PT:
- EdgeHealth (Elena / it_ops): confirm CIDRs + BGP ASN by Mon 20 Mar EOD; confirm NOC will run capture.
- Redwood (Marcus): provision mutual TLS test endpoint + share certs by Mon 20 Mar EOD.
- Redwood (Karthik): share load generator config and test harness repo link by Mon 20 Mar EOD.
- Redwood (Sean): create INF-9831 JIRA and attach runbook + correlation playbook.

Success criteria for the run (pass/fail):
- Pass: sustained 350 RPS with 100 concurrent streams and p95 client-to-model streaming latency <= 60 ms, or if we hit 50 ms p95 that's a stretch win.
- Fail/Actionable: p95 > 75 ms — collect pcaps + traceroutes, then reconvene for remediation steps.

I'll host a 30-minute readout Wed 22 Mar 10:00 PT to review captures and agree the path forward. Invites to follow.

Thanks — looking forward to the test.

--
